jobs.title: Support Counselor - ECM (Lead Care Manager)
jobs.description:
Lead Care Manager (ECM Support Counselor) 

Join our team as an ECM Support Counselor and take part in transforming the way Medi-Cal members with complex needs receive care and support.

As an ECM Support Counselor, you'll serve as the primary point of contact for Medi-Cal members enrolled in Enhanced Care Management (ECM). You will conduct outreach research across healthcare, community-based, and social-service settings throughout the San Francisco Bay Area to identify opportunities for connecting with and enrolling new client-members. You'll develop trusting relationships with members and provide comprehensive, individualized care management that addresses medical, behavioral health, and health-related social needs.

Working primarily in the community, you'll coordinate with health care providers, social service agencies, community organizations, and other members of the care team to ensure members receive the right services at the right time.

This is a full-time, benefited role with significant community-based work. The position requires flexibility to meet members where they live and receive services, including homes, health care settings, community centers, and other community locations. The ideal candidate is compassionate, organized, has strong public speaking and presentation skills, with the ability to communicate clearly and effectively with individuals or community groups, comfortable working in community-based settings, and culturally responsive and can support to individuals and families from diverse backgrounds.

About Alternative Family Services

Alternative Family Services is a Foster Family, Adoption and Mental Health Agency that has been serving abused and neglected children in our community since 1973. Our mission is to support vulnerable children and families in need of stability, safety, and well-being in communities. We provide a wide range of foster, adoption, mental health and transition-aged youth services in English and Spanish. We have eight locations throughout the Bay Area and over 200 employees. We celebrate diversity, equal opportunity, and excellence.

Responsibilities And What You’ll Do

Build relationships with community-based, social service, healthcare and other partner organizations throughout the San Francisco Bay Area to increase awareness of ECM services and generate new client-member enrollment. Identify and engage with community-based, social-service or healthcare organizations to generate new client-member enrollment and strengthen community partnerships Plan, coordinate and participate in community outreach events to increase awareness and enrolment of ECM services, foster relationships with prospective clients, and generate new client-member enrollment Serve as the member’s primary point of contact, providing individualized and comprehensive care managementDevelop person-centered care plans in partnership with members, their families or support systems, and the care teamMeet with client-members in their homes and communities to assess needs, provide support, and help remove barriers to careHelp client-members navigate health care and social service systems and connect them to appropriate providers and community resources across multiple systemsCoordinate referrals and follow up to ensure client-members successfully access recommended servicesMaintain regular communication with health plans, providers, community-based organizations, and other members of the interdisciplinary care teamAdvocate for members and help ensure their preferences, goals and needs remain central to their careMaintain accurate and timely documentation in accordance with organizational, Medi-Cal, and health plan requirementsMaintain confidentiality and compliance with HIPAA and applicable privacy standardsMonitor member progress and update care plans as needs and circumstances changeParticipate in care team meetings, case consultations, and other activities designed to improve coordination and outcomesRespond appropriately to urgent member needs and help connect members to crisis or emergency resources when necessary


Qualifications

Ability to obtain and maintain fingerprint and government and Agency required background clearancesCPR/First Aid certificationValid California driver’s license with an acceptable driving record, auto insurance showing as an insured driver on the policy and vehicle registrationA bachelor’s degree in a social science related field; or an associate degree in a social science related field and have at least six months experience in working with emotionally disturbed children or children who have a serious behavioral problem; or at least two years of experience working with emotionally disturbed children or children who have a serious behavioral problem, and who demonstrate a combination of education, skills, and experienceExperience providing case management, care coordination, social services, behavioral health services, health care services, or related support to individuals with complex needsExperience as an outreach coordinator and comfortability with public speakingKnowledge of county and community resources and the ability to connect members to social service programsStrong interpersonal and communication skillsExperience working with individuals experiencing complex medical, behavioral health, housing, food insecurity, or other social needsAbility to maintain accurate documentation and manage multiple cases, deadlines, and follow-up activitiesAbility to work independently while collaborating effectively with an interdisciplinary care teamCommitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, cultural humility, and person-centered careAble to interact with co-workers, county representatives, and other treatment team members as part of a cooperative teamPossess a high level of integrity, honesty and strong work ethicExperience working with Medi-Cal members or within a Medi-Cal managed care environment preferredExperience working with electronic health

jobs.title: Housing Specialist
jobs.description:
## About the International Rescue Committee

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions.

## The Role: UHP Housing Specialist

The UHP Housing Specialist secures and coordinates the furnishing of safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for newly arriving humanitarian parolees and refugees and provides related logistical support. This role works with staff, clients, and community partners to stabilize humanitarian parolee/refugee and client households by connecting them with long-term resources for low-income and designated affordable housing opportunities. In coordination with the UHP Team, the Housing Specialist locates housing for UHP clients and other vulnerable populations. The position also participates in program planning and service development through teams, committees, and work groups as required. The UHP Housing Specialist operates under moderate supervision with latitude for independent judgment and initiative. **This position has an end date of September 30, 2027.**

## What You'll Do

- Identify and secure safe, sanitary, and affordable housing for newly arriving refugees in compliance with established program requirements.

- Conduct ongoing outreach to current and potential landlords and property managers, building strong working relationships to increase access to housing for refugee families and coordinate client home repair requests.

- Collaborate effectively with coworkers and partner organizations to support a positive resettlement experience.

- Coordinate logistics of housing set-ups including ordering furniture and supplies, arranging delivery, arranging utility hook-ups, facilitating lease signings and renewals, arranging payments, and conducting home safety inspections.

- Implement a high-quality procurement protocol including researching potential new vendors, following appropriate financial and purchasing procedures, and maintaining required documentation.

- Deliver orientations to clients independently or in collaboration with housing caseworkers; may support other pre- and post-arrival activities such as airport pick-ups.

- Satisfy recordkeeping requirements.

- Use personal, insured vehicle and/or public transportation (where available) to travel and transport clients and materials as needed throughout the service delivery area.

- May train and lead the activities of support staff, volunteers, and interns.

- Other duties as assigned.

## Who You Are

**Education and Experience:**

- Bachelor’s degree

- Minimum of 1 year of housing-related professional experience required

- Experience working with refugee and/or immigrant populations preferred

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Strong relationship building, diplomacy, and networking skills; ability to effectively build internal and external relationships

- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multi-cultural environment

- Proven ability to contribute both independently and as a key team member

- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to multi-task, prioritize duties, and manage time effectively

- Superb organization, planning, and logistical skills

- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product

- Ability to regularly lift approximately 50 lbs

- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in Ukrainian and/or Russian language(s) spoken by IRC’s clients is preferred

- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes

- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle

## Work Setting

A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and field time within the service delivery area to perform the above responsibilities. May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

## Compensation

$26.00 to $27.00 per hour. Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

## Benefits

IRC offers a comprehensive and competitive benefits package. Highlights include:

- 10 paid sick leave days

- 10 U.S. holidays

- 20-25 generous paid time off days based on role and tenure

- Medical insurance starting at $163/month

- Dental starting at $6.50/month

- Vision starting at $5/month

- Flexible spending accounts (healthcare, dependent care, and commuter)

- 403(b) retirement savings plan with employer match (immediate vesting) along with a non-elective employer contribution based on age and years of service (3-year vesting)

- Disability and life insurance

- Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering confidential counseling and support services for employees and their families

## Professional Standards

All IRC workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in the IRC Way

- Standards for Professional Conduct: Integrity, Service, Equality, and Accountability. The IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation.

## Equal Opportunity

IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientatio

jobs.title: Interim Housing Case Manager
jobs.description:
The Case Manager provides intensive, individualized case management to individuals and families

residing in scattered-site interim housing throughout Ventura County. Participants include families

with children and Transitional Age Youth (TAY), with household needs potentially spanning

behavioral health, physical health, child and youth development, education, employment, income,

benefits, childcare, family functioning, and other areas affecting housing stability.

The Case Manager works with each household from entry with the goal of achieving a timely and

successful transition to permanent housing. Through comprehensive assessment, individualized

service planning, frequent engagement, resource coordination, and close collaboration with

Housing Navigators and other service providers, the Case Manager helps households address

immediate needs, reduce barriers to permanent housing, increase income and stability, and

develop the skills and resources necessary to successfully assume the responsibilities of a

permanent tenancy.

The position requires a family-centered approach that recognizes the needs of the household as a

whole while ensuring that the distinct needs of children, youth, TAY, parents, and other household

members are appropriately identified and addressed.

POSITION TITLE: Intensive Case Management Program: Case Manager

FLSA STATUS: Non-exempt

Property Focus: This position works with people who have experienced homelessness. It is a full-time position working in Long Beach.

To ensure resident safety, all staff who work directly with residents undergo background checks and fingerprinting.

Hiring range: $23.69 to $27.87 per hour

Note: The pay range is included in this posting to provide transparency and to reflect the potential for future compensation growth within the organization. New hires are placed within the hiring range based on their qualifications, experience, and alignment with the internal equity of existing staff members. Exceptions are considered only in rare cases where a candidate possesses highly specialized skills or expertise that are difficult to find in the market and are directly aligned with the position description.

Benefits Include: Medical/ Dental/ Vision; 401(k) with match; life insurance; long term disability coverage; medical and dependent care FSA.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Case Manager position for Linc Housing will be part of the Intensive Case Management Services team that will work with formerly homeless individuals with chronic medical conditions and co-occurring disorders. This position will report directly to the Senior Case Manager of ICMS and is responsible for the coordination of services utilizing best practices such as motivational interviewing, harm reduction, critical time intervention and stages of change. The sole function of Linc Housing’s Intensive case management services program is to mitigate the risk of individuals losing their housing by enhancing their ability to problem solve, use effective coping skills and manage and self-coordinate own care. In addition, the Case Manager will work closely with families, including children as well as a variety of partners such as property management, housing locators, third party service providers, and other Linc staff.

jobs.title: Housing Navigator at Koinonia Family Services Temecula, CA
jobs.description:
Housing Navigator job at Koinonia Family Services. Temecula, CA. Job Details 



 Description 

 Do you want to make a positive difference in the lives of vulnerable individuals in your community? If yes, consider joining the team at Koinonia Family Services as a  Housing Navigator  in our Community Supports program in Temecula, also serving parts of San Bernardino and San Diego. This part-time position helps individuals experiencing or at-risk of homelessness access safe and stable housing by guiding them through housing navigation, benefit advocacy, and service coordination. We are especially seeking candidates with strong bilingual or multilingual proficiency to support our diverse client base. 

 Opportunity Highlights 

 Community Supports is a Medi-Cal benefit offered under California’s CalAIM initiative, designed to address social determinants of health that impact well-being—such as housing instability. The Housing Navigator plays a key role in delivering Housing Transition Navigation Services, a Community Supports benefit that helps eligible individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness find and maintain safe, stable housing. This includes conducting individualized housing assessments, developing personalized support plans, securing rental subsidies and documentation, and coordinating move-in logistics. The Housing Navigator also educates clients on tenant rights and provides ongoing advocacy to promote housing retention. This position serves clients throughout the San Diego area and collaborates closely with Enhanced Care Management (ECM) providers and community partners to ensure integrated and person-centered support. 

 The House Navigator Opportunity Includes 

 A job with purpose – help individuals move from instability to housing success  Hourly pay rate: $23.00 per hour to start, or higher with prior housing navigation or case management experience  Benefits include: paid time off (PTO), paid holidays, and participation in our 401k plan  Flexible, part-time schedule (20–25 hours/week) with remote work between in-person visits  Mileage reimbursement for business-related travel  Work with a supportive team and mission-driven organization  Field-based work in the greater San Diego area 

 This role offers 20-25 hours per week, with shifts typically running from early afternoon to early evening. The position is primarily remote, involving client visits in the field and occasional in-person meetings at our office in San Diego. 

 Key Responsibilities 

 Under the supervision of the Community Supports Program Manager, you will: 

 Conduct housing assessments and develop individualized housing support plans (IHSPs) Assist individuals in identifying and securing housing options  Help complete housing applications and gather documentation (e.g., ID, SS card, rental history) Match clients to rental subsidy programs and one-time housing assistance resources  Advocate with landlords and educate clients on tenant rights and responsibilities  Support the logistics of moving and coordinate necessary transportation or home modifications  Coordinate services with ECM providers, community resources, and county homelessness systems  Submit service authorization requests to Managed Care Plans and document all services in an EHR  Facilitate transitions to long-term tenancy support services when appropriate 

 Qualifications 

 A strong desire to support people in finding and maintaining stable housing  A compassionate, non-judgmental nature, with the ability to build trust and rapport with vulnerable populations  Bilingual or multilingual abilities are a plus  Minimum 2 years of experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness or providing housing-related case management preferred  Understanding of housing systems, rental assistance programs (e.g., Section 8), and tenant rights  Familiarity with best practices such as Housing First, Harm Reduction, Motivational Interviewing, and Trauma-Informed Care  Ability to maintain accurate records and submit required documentation for Medi-Cal services  Strong interpersonal skills, cultural sensitivity, and the ability to build trust with vulnerable populations  Ability to work independently and manage a caseload  Valid driver’s license, auto insurance, and reliable transportation 

 We are seeking bilingual or multilingual candidates who have at least two years of related work experience in social work, case management, community engagement or customer service. High school graduate or GED required. Prior experience as a community health worker, peer support specialist, medical assistant or similar role is a plus. 

 Join Our Team 

 At Koinonia Family Services, we foster a supportive and inclusive work environment. In a recent employee satisfaction survey, 95% of employees reported strong coworker relationships, 96% were satisfied with their supervisors, and 94% felt respected at work. As a trauma-informed agency, we prioritize a person-centered treatment philosophy. Join us in making a meaningful impact on youth and families, bringing hope and healing to those in need. 

 Important Note 

 Qualified candidates must complete a criminal background clearance through the California Department of Justice and FBI to ensure eligibility for employment, as well as a pre-employment physical and TB test. This position requires a valid driver’s license, auto insurance and reliable transportation as driving is an essential job function. Housing Navigators are responsible for tasks such as visiting client homes, attending in-person meetings, and engaging with community partners, often in locations not easily accessible by alternative transportation methods. The nature of these responsibilities necessitates the ability to drive to ensure timely, reliable, confidential and effective support for the individuals we serve. Koinonia Family Services is an equal-opportunity employer.

DESCRIPTIONThe Department of Medicine is responsible for fulfilling the teaching, research, and clinical missions of the University of California, San Diego and employs 486+ full-time salaried faculty members and 100+ academic appointees. Staff personnel include 600+ staff in 9 bargaining units, students, and volunteers. There are 250 clinical faculty practicing at multiple sites.

Under the general supervision of the social work supervisor, the Trans Health Project (THP) Case Manager provides comprehensive, trauma-informed, gender-affirming, and culturally responsive case management support services to Black and Latina transgender women, prioritizing participants enrolled in the THP initiative research project with UCSD. This position supports Black and Latina transgender women experiencing barriers to health care, HIV prevention and treatment services, housing stability, economic security, behavioral health services, and other social determinants of health.

Using a participant-centered and strengths-based approach, the THP Case Manager assists participants in identifying goals, advocating for their needs across systems of care, accessing gender-affirming services, and addressing barriers to overall health and well-being. The position provides care coordination, resource linkage, and service advocacy, while working collaboratively with community partners and research collaborators to support participant engagement, retention, and connection to services, while ensuring confidentiality and compliance with organizational, funder, and research requirements. The ideal candidate possesses experience working with transgender and BIPOC communities, demonstrates cultural humility and responsiveness, and has knowledge of the unique challenges impacting Black and Latina transgender women. Spanish-language proficiency is strongly preferred.

Experience working with the LGBTQ community and persons living with or affected by HIV infection, particularly young Latina and Black transgender women, in San Diego County.

Fluency in English.

Must demonstrate competence in working with diverse populations.

Knowledge of person-first language and inclusive language used in sexual, gender, and racial/ethnic minority populations.

Must demonstrate competence in using strength-based, trauma-informed, and motivational interviewing techniques.   

Experience working with bilingual (English and Spanish) communities.

Must have access to reliable transportation.

Knowledge of HIV transmission, care, prevention, and pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP.

Housing Navigator job at Koinonia Family Services. Temecula, CA. Job Details 



 Description 

 Do you want to make a positive difference in the lives of vulnerable individuals in your community? If yes, consider joining the team at Koinonia Family Services as a  Housing Navigator  in our Community Supports program in Temecula, also serving parts of San Bernardino and San Diego. This part-time position helps individuals experiencing or at-risk of homelessness access safe and stable housing by guiding them through housing navigation, benefit advocacy, and service coordination. We are especially seeking candidates with strong bilingual or multilingual proficiency to support our diverse client base. 

 Opportunity Highlights 

 Community Supports is a Medi-Cal benefit offered under California’s CalAIM initiative, designed to address social determinants of health that impact well-being—such as housing instability. The Housing Navigator plays a key role in delivering Housing Transition Navigation Services, a Community Supports benefit that helps eligible individuals experiencing or at risk of homelessness find and maintain safe, stable housing. This includes conducting individualized housing assessments, developing personalized support plans, securing rental subsidies and documentation, and coordinating move-in logistics. The Housing Navigator also educates clients on tenant rights and provides ongoing advocacy to promote housing retention. This position serves clients throughout the San Diego area and collaborates closely with Enhanced Care Management (ECM) providers and community partners to ensure integrated and person-centered support. 

 The House Navigator Opportunity Includes 

 A job with purpose – help individuals move from instability to housing success  Hourly pay rate: $23.00 per hour to start, or higher with prior housing navigation or case management experience  Benefits include: paid time off (PTO), paid holidays, and participation in our 401k plan  Flexible, part-time schedule (20–25 hours/week) with remote work between in-person visits  Mileage reimbursement for business-related travel  Work with a supportive team and mission-driven organization  Field-based work in the greater San Diego area 

 This role offers 20-25 hours per week, with shifts typically running from early afternoon to early evening. The position is primarily remote, involving client visits in the field and occasional in-person meetings at our office in San Diego. 

 Key Responsibilities 

 Under the supervision of the Community Supports Program Manager, you will: 

 Conduct housing assessments and develop individualized housing support plans (IHSPs) Assist individuals in identifying and securing housing options  Help complete housing applications and gather documentation (e.g., ID, SS card, rental history) Match clients to rental subsidy programs and one-time housing assistance resources  Advocate with landlords and educate clients on tenant rights and responsibilities  Support the logistics of moving and coordinate necessary transportation or home modifications  Coordinate services with ECM providers, community resources, and county homelessness systems  Submit service authorization requests to Managed Care Plans and document all services in an EHR  Facilitate transitions to long-term tenancy support services when appropriate 

 Qualifications 

 A strong desire to support people in finding and maintaining stable housing  A compassionate, non-judgmental nature, with the ability to build trust and rapport with vulnerable populations  Bilingual or multilingual abilities are a plus  Minimum 2 years of experience working with individuals experiencing homelessness or providing housing-related case management preferred  Understanding of housing systems, rental assistance programs (e.g., Section 8), and tenant rights  Familiarity with best practices such as Housing First, Harm Reduction, Motivational Interviewing, and Trauma-Informed Care  Ability to maintain accurate records and submit required documentation for Medi-Cal services  Strong interpersonal skills, cultural sensitivity, and the ability to build trust with vulnerable populations  Ability to work independently and manage a caseload  Valid driver’s license, auto insurance, and reliable transportation 

 We are seeking bilingual or multilingual candidates who have at least two years of related work experience in social work, case management, community engagement or customer service. High school graduate or GED required. Prior experience as a community health worker, peer support specialist, medical assistant or similar role is a plus. 

 Join Our Team 

 At Koinonia Family Services, we foster a supportive and inclusive work environment. In a recent employee satisfaction survey, 95% of employees reported strong coworker relationships, 96% were satisfied with their supervisors, and 94% felt respected at work. As a trauma-informed agency, we prioritize a person-centered treatment philosophy. Join us in making a meaningful impact on youth and families, bringing hope and healing to those in need. 

 Important Note 

 Qualified candidates must complete a criminal background clearance through the California Department of Justice and FBI to ensure eligibility for employment, as well as a pre-employment physical and TB test. This position requires a valid driver’s license, auto insurance and reliable transportation as driving is an essential job function. Housing Navigators are responsible for tasks such as visiting client homes, attending in-person meetings, and engaging with community partners, often in locations not easily accessible by alternative transportation methods. The nature of these responsibilities necessitates the ability to drive to ensure timely, reliable, confidential and effective support for the individuals we serve. Koinonia Family Services is an equal-opportunity employer.

Staff personnel include 600+ staff in 9 bargaining units, students, and volunteers. There are 250 clinical faculty practicing at multiple sites.

Under the general supervision of the social work supervisor, the Trans Health Project (THP) Case Manager provides comprehensive, trauma-informed, gender-affirming, and culturally responsive case management support services to Black and Latina transgender women, prioritizing participants enrolled in the THP initiative research project with UCSD. This position supports Black and Latina transgender women experiencing barriers to health care, HIV prevention and treatment services, housing stability, economic security, behavioral health services, and other social determinants of health.

Using a participant-centered and strengths-based approach, the THP Case Manager assists participants in identifying goals, advocating for their needs across systems of care, accessing gender-affirming services, and addressing barriers to overall health and well-being. The position provides care coordination, resource linkage, and service advocacy, while working collaboratively with community partners and research collaborators to support participant engagement, retention, and connection to services, while ensuring confidentiality and compliance with organizational, funder, and research requirements. The ideal candidate possesses experience working with transgender and BIPOC communities, demonstrates cultural humility and responsiveness, and has knowledge of the unique challenges impacting Black and Latina transgender women. Spanish-language proficiency is strongly preferred.
